name: Sovereign debt stress
summary: French 10-year yield held at 4.74% on 27 Nov, near a two-month low, ahead of an S&P rating review; no failed G7 auction
state: The French 10-year yield held at 4.74% on 27 Nov ahead of a scheduled S&P review of France's rating, after falling below 4.75% on 25 Nov to its lowest since 9 Nov (Trading Economics). It had climbed towards 4.9% on 13 Nov and reached its highest since 2002 in early October (FXStreet, 2 Oct). Searches on 28 Nov found no published S&P decision, no confirmed France–Bund spread above 150bp, no failed G7 auction and no emergency central-bank buying, so Watch holds on still-elevated long-dated yields.
for_you: Holders of French government debt and French borrowers are most exposed to higher long-term rates. A rating cut tends to push yields up for a time, and higher state borrowing costs can feed through to mortgage and business lending rates.
rubric_hit: Watch: G7 long-dated yields still elevated (French 10y 4.74% after Oct 24-year high); no failed auction or France–Bund > 150bp

sources.title: Trading Economics — French Bond Yields Rise as ECB Rate Hike Bets Grow (with updates to 27 Nov)
FXStreet — France's 10-year yield hits highest since 2002

why: When big governments struggle to borrow, it raises everyone's costs and can force sudden austerity or money-printing.
drivers: Deficits, auction demand, ratings actions, political shocks, long-end yields.

rubric.alert: Failed G7 auction, emergency central-bank purchases, France–Bund > 150bp, or Italy–Bund > 250bp.
rubric.watch: G7 30-year yields at multi-decade highs, a G7 downgrade, or France–Bund 80–150bp / Italy–Bund 150–250bp.
rubric.normal: Auctions orderly; France–Bund spread < 80bp; Italy–Bund < 150bp; no G7 downgrades this month.
